sessionTitle: Building Agents You Can Trust on Windows

announcements.name: Three Windows agent primitives: identity, containment, manageability
announcements.shortDescription: Windows treats agents as a new class of user with a distinct security principal, an enforced isolation boundary, and IT-governable policies.
announcements.longDescription: As the definition of a "user" expands to include agents acting on a person's behalf, Windows is introducing three key platform capabilities so agents can be treated as a new class of user and run safely and reliably. The first is agent identity, giving the agent an identity distinct from the human user. The second is containment, running agents in a controlled environment where their blast radius is limited rather than granting full access to all files and data. The third is manageability, allowing an IT admin to deploy, monitor, govern, and enforce policies dictating what an agent can and cannot do.

announcements.name: Microsoft Execution Containers (MXC) Library
announcements.shortDescription: A cross-platform, declarative library that dynamically composes a right-sized container per agent action by matching developer, user, and IT policy against available OS primitives.
announcements.longDescription: The Microsoft Execution Containers (MXC) Library is introduced to create containers based on policy, providing an isolation boundary proportionate to the risk and action an agent performs. Developers and agents declare the security requirements of the agent and its individual actions, and the library compiles those and matches them against system policies and policies defined by IT through familiar deployment, management, and monitoring tools. Once a match occurs, the MXC library examines the native OS platform primitives and assembles the right container for the job, a process called dynamic composition. This enables least-privilege enforcement where each action runs in its own sandbox with policy defining just what it can do.

announcements.name: Dynamic composition across container sizes
announcements.shortDescription: MXC scales from small processes to VMs, Firecracker-style micro VMs, and cloud PCs, spanning Windows, WSL, and Linux.
announcements.longDescription: Dynamic composition means that when an agent runs there is no fixed container; the MXC library creates the container on the fly by combining the definition of the application or action, the user's consent and permissions, and the policy defined by IT into a container configuration. It then looks at the available operating system primitives to craft the appropriate container. MXC is a full cross-platform library spanning Windows, WSL, and Linux that can scale from tiny small processes to VMs, micro VMs, Firecracker-style micro VMs, all the way up to cloud-based PCs. This allows a security boundary that is designed and proportionate to the task to be accomplished.

announcements.name: Sandbox shipping out-of-box in GitHub Copilot CLI and SDK
announcements.shortDescription: Built with the Windows team and currently behind an experimental flag, with general availability and default-on planned for the future.
announcements.longDescription: Through collaboration with the Windows team, the Copilot CLI and SDK can now ship a sandbox out of the box, currently available under an experimental flag and planned to become a default-on solution at GA in the future. This moves the agent to a fully isolated state where the entire agent can be placed inside safe environments and allowed to execute freely, enabling a wider range of jobs end to end without directly supervising the agent. Users can access slash sandbox commands to turn it on and off and to configure policy, including file system configuration that protects working directories. The demos show enabling file system protections so that a request to delete all desktop files triggers a permissions prompt.

announcements.name: Agent 365 native integration via MXC
announcements.shortDescription: Agents built with MXC gain integration with Microsoft Defender, Entra, and Intune (in preview) so security and IT teams can constrain local agents.
announcements.longDescription: An additional benefit of using MXC to build agents is Agent 365 native integration, which enables agents running on Windows to start secure and stay secure. This integration provides access to the full ecosystem, including Defender, Entra [inferred], and Intune (in preview), whose protections allow security and IT teams to constrain and secure local agents and make them run more securely in enterprise contexts. The capabilities were built working closely with the Copilot team and the broader ecosystem, including partners like OpenAI, Manus, NVIDIA, and others. This complements the summary that agents on Windows should run identified, contained, and managed.
